$description: The assistant — the Inspector dock's fourth tab — as a Jx document over the kit. The adapter (`panels/ai-panel.ts`) keeps every decision: which pane is showing, what the chat state holds, how a tool call turned out, what a turn changed, which `Assistant:` records the registry offers and what a send does. This document is handed one flat projection — rows already keyed by message id, chips already told their outcome, commands already resolved to a glyph, a label, a tooltip and whether they are refused — and it draws it. Nothing here parses a tool's arguments, reads the write ledger or asks the registry a question. Two islands: `[part="md"]` is filled with sanitized model output by `ai-chat/chat-markdown.ts`, and `[part="composer-picker"]` receives the model picker's own mounted surface — both through `onNodeCreated` (specs/studio-ui-guidelines.md §9.4). The transcript is a keyed `$map` on the message id and nothing below a row is keyed by position, so a token appended to the tail reconciles one text node instead of rebuilding the list under the reader's caret.

style.$description: Fifty-odd `.ai-*` rules in `styles/shell.css`, keyed on `part` and carried here rather than moved: the stylesheet is outside this change's blast radius, so those rules are left behind as dead text for a central sweep. Three Spectrum names could not come with the declarations and are the kit's instead, at the same values — `--spectrum-font-size-50` (11px) is `--jx-text-sm`, `--spectrum-font-size-75` (12px) is `--jx-text-md`, and the 10px literals are `--jx-text-xs`. Four things changed on purpose. A SESSION ROW IS A BUTTON: it was a `<div>` with a click handler and no role, so the chat history could not be reached from the keyboard at all. THE TRANSCRIPT AND THE IMPORT LOG ARE FOCUSABLE, because a scroll region a pointer can reach and a keyboard cannot is one a keyboard reader cannot read. THE TYPING INDICATOR ANNOUNCES ITSELF as a status rather than being three decorative spans. And THE COMPOSER GROWS WITHOUT MEASURING: `field-sizing: content` over a one-row box replaces the per-keystroke `scrollHeight` write the lit composer ran, with `rows` as the height an engine without it keeps.

& [part=\"tokens\"].$description: The conversation's share of the model's context. Quiet until it matters: past half the window the assistant starts dropping the oldest turns, and this is the only thing that says so.

& [part=\"messages\"].$description: THE chat scroller — bounded by `min-height: 0` at every flex level above it. It carries `tabindex="0"` because a scrollable region a pointer can reach and a keyboard cannot is one a keyboard reader cannot read at all, and the ring below is what that costs.

& [part=\"md\"].$description: The island `panels/ai-chat/chat-markdown.ts` fills — the app's ONE injection sink, and the markup reaching it has been through `markdownToHtml` and the Trusted Types policy that asserts it did. The document renders the host node and nothing inside it (specs/studio-ui-guidelines.md §9.4).

& [part=\"ask\"].$description: A question the assistant is waiting on. Deliberately louder than a tool chip and quieter than an error: it is the one thing in the transcript that will not proceed without the reader.

& [part=\"import\"].$description: An import, under the chip that started it. It reports for minutes and then stays: the summary line is the run's outcome once it has one, and the log below is a scroller the reader owns — it follows the newest line until they scroll away from it, and stops following while they read.

& [part=\"import-count\"].$description: How many lines are folded away, so a collapsed run still says how much it has to show.

& [part=\"import-log-line\"].$description: Wraps rather than ellipses: a phase line names a page, a count or a file, and the end of it is usually the part worth reading.

& [part=\"changes\"].$description: The turn's changed-files summary. Collapsed by default because the headline is the part that must never be missed; the list is for when it is.

& [part=\"change-caveat\"].$description: The undo caveat, rendered to the person holding the undo chord rather than appended to the model-facing tool summary.

& [part=\"composer-input\"].$description: A textarea the surface owns outright rather than a `jx-textfield`, for the reason `palette.json` gives about its own combobox: the field needs a ceiling (120px, then it scrolls) and the kit field exposes no token for one, so binding it would mean styling another component's `[part="input"]` from outside. `field-sizing: content` is what grows it — no measurement and no handler per keystroke, where the lit composer wrote `scrollHeight` back on every input.

& [part=\"composer-note\"].$description: The chat-only-model note, under the picker that caused it. Advisory weight on purpose: the assistant still answers, it just cannot edit.

& [part=\"setup\"].$description: The in-panel residue of the retired credentials gate: one sentence and the action that fixes it, between the transcript and the composer.

& [part=\"session-open\"].$description: A BUTTON, where the lit row was a `<div>` with a click handler and no role: the chat history could not be reached from the keyboard at all.

@(forced-colors: active).$description: Every author colour is replaced by one from the user's palette in forced colours, so the washes behind a user bubble, a question card and an error collapse into the page. A border is what is left, and each is given a palette colour of its own so the three still read apart.

onscroll.description: The reader moved the transcript. The adapter records whether they are still at the newest message; a reader who has scrolled up is reading something, and pinning them back on every token is what makes a live transcript unreadable.

shown.textContent: Ask the assistant to build or edit this page — it can add sections, restyle elements, and wire up components.

unanswered.textContent: This question was still open when the session was reloaded — reply below to carry on.

true.textContent: written to disk — undo cannot reach it

children.textContent: No AI provider is connected yet.

onkeydown.description: Enter sends and Shift+Enter opens a line, unless an IME is mid-composition — the one key a chat composer owns.
